learning.why: Teacher’s dance example and the ghee melting recall helped the child confidently use the rule about no new substance forming being the mark of a physical change.

end.summary: Defined physical change as no new substance, with changes in shape, size, or state.
end.parentNote: Ananya practised identifying physical changes using dancing, cutting and folding paper, melting ghee, and freezing water, and chemical changes using roasting chapati and cooking an egg. They explained the method by checking whether a new substance formed and whether the original material remained. Ananya asked whether curd or cooked chapati could return to their original forms; this reversibility mix-up was corrected later through the water-and-ice example. At home, ask Ananya to sort five everyday changes into physical or chemical and give one reason for each.
